g.text: Each component is a module in every tree: rust/src/<m>.rs, python/src/aero1553/<m>.py, cpp/src/<m>.cpp (Python spells a few differently: filters, exceptions, logger).
tests/conformance/ holds the three byte-identical on CSV output. The platform layer is C++ only. Circled numbers refer to the notes at the bottom.
produced by decode, read by every later stage
Rust: MieError enum + kind() | Python: Aero1553Error class tree | C++: MieError
sync: NoValidRecords, FirstRecordTruncated, HomogeneousPayload | invariants: record error (strict)
platform -- cpp/include/mie/platform.hpp, the only C++ code that touches the OS
map the input, atomic output, directory enumeration (--glob), binary stdout, path identity

text.tspan: 1. find_first_record: scan for the first valid record, <= 64 KB
2. validate_record: shape probe of the candidate
3. look-ahead: the next N-1 records must also validate
(N = lookahead_records, default 2, L2-SYN-026)
4. recover_sync: after a mid-file failure, 2-byte steps, <= 64 KB
Homogeneous payloads (all-zero, all-0xFFFF) that would
otherwise pass validation are rejected: HomogeneousPayload.
L2-SYN-020..025 and L2-SYN-027 check each decoded record
against the MIL-STD-1553 transaction shape.
A violated rule: strict mode surfaces a record error
(PayloadError); lenient mode logs a WARN and skips the record.
InvariantSeverity::AnomalyWarn findings log a WARN and keep it.
Errored records skip these checks: their payload is
truncated by definition.
1. Reject input == output (L2-WRT-014).
2. --no-clobber: reported early, ENFORCED at commit by a
non-replacing move (L2-WRT-017, L2-WRT-023).
3. Write <dest>.aero1553.tmp.<pid>.<counter>.<nanos> beside
the destination, exclusive create (L3-WRT-001).
4. Clean exit: commit renames the temp file onto the destination.
5. Error + --allow-partial: commit_partial -> <output>.partial (L2-WRT-016).
6. Error otherwise: the temp file is removed (L2-WRT-016).
Main output commits before errors output on every path (L2-WRT-019).
Inputs: positionals / --manifest / --glob, at most 256 (L2-MRG-001).
Min-heap keyed (IRIG microseconds, input index, sequence); at most
one record per open input, so memory is O(files) (L2-MRG-002).
Every input must be calendar-locked IRIG: Standard, freerun-leading
or mixed sets are rejected before any output (exit 6, L2-MRG-003).
DELTA is per input file by default; --delta-scope global
recomputes it on the merged timeline (L2-MRG-005).
A backward step within one input: WARN, or NonMonotonicInput in
strict mode; never re-sorted (L2-MRG-006).
--collapse-duplicates drops cross-recorder duplicates (L2-MRG-007),
capped by max_collapse_survivors (L2-MRG-008).
Buffers one run of CONSECUTIVE equal-TIME_STAMP records and
stable-sorts it by (RT, subaddress, direction), receive before
transmit (L2-WRT-021). Never reorders across a timestamp boundary.
Records with no Command Word (SPURIOUS_DATA) are pinned to the
record they followed, keeping a 0x2000 continuation adjacent.
Run length is capped by output.max_sort_group (default 4096); at
the cap the run is emitted in arrival order with one WARN
(L2-WRT-022). A cap of 1 disables reordering.
Last stage on BOTH the single-file and merge paths; not applied
to the dump subcommand.
1. CLI flags (--no-clobber, --allow-partial, --separate-errors,
--include-rts, ...)
2. TOML config file (--config)
3. Built-in defaults
Applied as load_config() then with_overrides().
0 complete, partial-recovered, --allow-partial, broken pipe,
empty recording
1 runtime or decode error (record or file I/O)
2 no records: NoValidRecords, HomogeneousPayload,
TimestampFormatMismatch (strict)
3 partial-unrecoverable (no --allow-partial)
4 usage error
5 configuration error
6 merge-incompatible inputs
